- 56 observations over a baseline of 282.7 days
- median reported uncertainty: 2.51 m/s

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Initial hypothesis: a 1-planet system with the dominant signal at 188.49 d.

Why this period:
- It is by far the strongest peak (power 0.706) with extremely low approximate FAP (~4.7e-12).
- It is below the 282.7 d baseline, so it is at least somewhat constrained by the data.
- The nearby alternatives look more like relatives/aliases than independent planets:
  - 94.24 d is exactly the half-period harmonic.
  - 376.98 d is the double-period relative and is longer than the baseline, so poorly constrained.
  - 88.36 d is close to half of 176.7 d and plausibly part of the same long-period/harmonic structure rather than a separate secure planet.
- The other listed peaks are weak and have poor FAPs, many near 1 day or cadence-related regions, so they are not good planet candidates at this stage.

So the simplest supported model is:
- Planet b: P ≈ 188.49 d

Please fit a 1-planet Keplerian at ~188.5 d first, then inspect residuals to see whether any coherent signal remains that is not just an alias/harmonic of this long-period planet.
